actual_checks: Full exact report, literal prompt, provenance/source records and full transvection-criterion prior read. The new contribution uses the current image dichotomy for a Frobenius certificate and exact isogeny field degree; it differs from the prior abstract transvection sufficient condition.

Furio–Lombardo v2 Theorem 1.5 gives exactly GL_2 or the full nonsplit normalizer for non-CM rational elliptic curves and p>37. Theorem 1.6 excludes the index-three proper subgroup; merely containment would not suffice for the orbit conclusion, and the report explicitly uses equality.

For nonsplit Cartan matrices (a,epsilon*b;b,a), discriminant is 4 epsilon b^2, hence zero or nonsquare; matrices in the outer coset have trace zero. Thus a good Frobenius with nonzero trace and nonzero square discriminant excludes the normalizer and certifies surjectivity by the dichotomy. No finite search bound or universal existence of such a certificate is claimed.

Both possible full groups contain F_(p^2)^* acting transitively on P^1(F_p); every cyclic subgroup of E[p] therefore has orbit p+1. Its stabilizer fixed field has degree p+1 and quotient isogeny descent gives an isogeny there. Any K-defined cyclic p-isogeny has a G_K-stable kernel, so its minimal line field lies in K and p+1 divides [K:Q], even for non-Galois K. This is the degree of a kernel line rather than of a chosen nonzero torsion point. The full normalizer alternative and Serre uniformity remain unresolved.
